# Data
Load libraries
```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, # spatial
               here, 
               tidyverse, 
               rio, # for importing
               table1, # make table1
               lubridate,
               ncf, #correlation
               xtable, # export table1
               fuzzyjoin, # joining with some inexact
               spdep, # regression spatial
               tmap # spatial maps
               )
```

Read in shapefiles
```{r}
## Read in case shapefile - TIRS_SINAVE_22_23
sus <- st_read(dsn = here("data"), 
                 layer = "TIRS_SINAVE_22_23")
## Cluster shapefile
clusters <- st_read(dsn = here("data"),
                    layer = "Cluster final 2021 actualizado")
```

SINAVE raw data
```{r}
season21 <- here::here("data", "SINAVE_Data", 
                       "datos_abiertos_dengue_301221.csv") %>%
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()

season22 <- here::here("data", "SINAVE_Data", 
                       "datos_abiertos_dengue_011222.csv") %>%
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()

season23 <- here::here("data", "SINAVE_Data", 
                       "datos_abiertos_dengue_061223.csv") %>%
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()
```


## Questions
```{r}
# are there suspected cases for both sources for both years?
table(sus$Source, sus$Year)

# diagnosis labels for each source
sinave <- sus %>% filter(Source=="SINAVE")
tirs <- sus %>% filter(Source=="TIRS")
unique(sinave$Diagnosis)
unique(tirs$Diagnosis)

# only dengue?
tirs_DENV <- tirs %>% filter(str_detect(Diagnosis, "DENV")) # 245 cases
table(tirs_DENV$Year, tirs_DENV$Diagnosis)
# what DENV diagnosis, for which years?
```
Ok now I have a dataset that has all the TIRS cases labeled by infection type 
WHICH WAS HARDER THAN I THOUGHT IT'D BE
```{r}
# all dengue cases from the TIRS trial
tirs_all_cases <- readRDS("all_cases_labeled.rds")
tirs_all_denv <- tirs_all_cases %>% 
  filter(denv_case == 1 | denv_zikv == 1 | denv_chikv == 1) # 327 (includes DENV coinfections)

# all dengue cases given to me in the one file
tirs_DENV # 245 

#ok? are these all ? mostly? the same people?
## i'll rbind select variables of each...
sub_trial_data <- tirs_all_denv %>% # 327 cases
  select(PPID, evnt_year, var6_symp_date, arm) %>% 
  rename(id = PPID,
         event_year = evnt_year,
         symp_onset = var6_symp_date,
         trial_arm = arm) %>% 
  mutate(source = "Trial Data")
sub_govt_data <- tirs_DENV %>% # 245 cases
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  select(ID, Year, Onset_symp, Arm_1TIRS) %>% 
  rename(id = ID,
         event_year = Year,
         symp_onset = Onset_symp,
         trial_arm = Arm_1TIRS) %>% 
  mutate(source = "MoH Data")
test_tirs_cases <- rbind(sub_trial_data, sub_govt_data)

# ok how can i make sure to only grab the non-duplicates?
tirs_all_denv %>% count(PPID) %>% #number of times an indv was infected w dengue
  count(n) # there are four IDs that have two events, two that have three

# which ones have multiple events
sub_govt_data %>% count(id) %>% filter(n > 1) # not just first events
tirs_all_denv %>% count(PPID) %>% 
  filter(n > 1)

# what about by year? # this works, all one year so group by that
tirs_all_denv %>% count(PPID, evnt_year) %>% #number of times an indv was infected w dengue
  count(n) 

test_tirs_cases %>% arrange(id, event_year) #some duplicates...
only_in_one <- anti_join(sub_trial_data, sub_govt_data, 
                         by = c("id", "event_year"))
# ok so all moh cases are included in the TIRS cases (so they're not extra ones
# picked up by the MoH that weren't picked up by the clinical trial)
# all extra cases are ones picked up by the trial
# 82 extra cases

tirs_all_denv %>% filter(PPID %in% only_in_one$id)
# uhhh all these are different trial arms, different block types (central vs.
# periphery)
```

### Dengue 2023 Outbreak
```{r}
# well, it's not like i can use too much from the extra 82 tirs cases since
# i don't have their location information
# so

# All cases, most of TIRS (missing 82), and more than the number of cases
# Natalie had for community/SINAVE
test <- sinave_block[,-c(1:11)]
denv23 <- cbind(sus, test)

denv23 <- denv23 %>% #674 cases
  filter((str_detect(Diagnosis, "DENV") | str_detect(Diagnosis, "DENGUE"))
         & Year == 2023) # only dengue, only 2023

# so....regression analysis now?
```

Regression?
Uhhh do cases within a cluster tend to occur closer together? That is, 
closer than expected under a null model of random placement inside that cluster
```{r}
# , warning=FALSE
yuc_pop <- read.csv("RESAGEBURB2020 - 31 Yucatán.csv")

# combine population size for each CVEGEO with the shapefile...all the CVEGEOs
# within the cluster...
yuc_cluster_pops <- yuc_pop %>% 
  mutate(CVE_ENT = as.character(ENTIDAD),
         CVE_MUN = paste0("0", MUN),
         CVE_LOC = paste0("000", LOC),
         CVE_AGEB = AGEB,
         CVE_MZA = ifelse(nchar(as.character(yuc_pop$MZA)) == 3, as.character(MZA),
                          ifelse(nchar(as.character(yuc_pop$MZA)) == 2, paste0("0", MZA),
                                 paste0("00", MZA))),
         CVEGEO = paste0(CVE_ENT, CVE_MUN, CVE_LOC, CVE_AGEB, CVE_MZA))
yuc_cluster_pops <- yuc_cluster_pops[-c(1:3),]
# population of those in the clusters...matching by CVEGEO this better be correct
trial_cluster_pops <- clusters %>% 
  left_join(yuc_cluster_pops, by = c("CVEGEO","CVE_ENT", "CVE_MUN", "CVE_LOC", 
                                     "CVE_AGEB", "CVE_MZA"))

# cases by tirs cluster...
cases_by_blockid <- denv23 %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  group_by(CLUSTER, MZTIRS) %>% 
  summarize(cases = n())
# population per tirs block/cluster 
pop_per_blockid <- trial_cluster_pops %>% # some with total pop = 0? from the 2020 census record?
  group_by(CLUSTER, MZTIRS) %>% 
  summarize(pop = sum(POBTOT))

# trial_cluster_pops %>% 
#   st_drop_geometry() %>% 
#   arrange(CLUSTER, MZTIRS) %>% 
#   filter(CLUSTER == 63 & MZTIRS == 28)

case_rate <- pop_per_blockid %>% # rates of DENV cases per TIRS block in 2023
  mutate(CLUSTER = as.numeric(CLUSTER)) %>% 
  full_join(cases_by_blockid, by = c("CLUSTER", "MZTIRS")) %>% 
  mutate(cases = ifelse(is.na(cases), 0, cases),
         rate = ifelse(pop == 0, 0, cases/pop),
         rate_pcnt = rate * 100)
# per cluster
pop_per_cluster <- pop_per_blockid %>%
  group_by(CLUSTER) %>% 
  summarize(cluster_pop = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE))
cases_by_cluster <- cases_by_blockid %>% 
  group_by(CLUSTER) %>% 
  summarize(cases_cluster = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE))
case_rate_cluster <- pop_per_cluster %>% 
  mutate(CLUSTER = as.numeric(CLUSTER)) %>% 
  left_join(cases_by_cluster, by = "CLUSTER") %>% 
  mutate(rate = ifelse(cluster_pop == 0, 
                       paste0("No recorded population for this cluster"), 
                       cases_cluster/cluster_pop),
         rate_pcnt = ifelse(rate == "No recorded population for this cluster", 
                            NA, as.numeric(rate)*100))

```

```{r}
# eeent - State Geostatistical Areas (no)
# eemun - Municipal Geostatistical Areas (no)
# eear - Basic Rural Geostatistical Areas (no)
# eel - Polygon of Urban and Rural Blocked Localities (no)
# eelpr - Rural Point Localities (probably not)
# eeti - Island Territory (probably not)
# eea - Basic Urban Geostatistical Areas (yeah kinda)
# eem - Block Polygons (yes oh my god) ///smaller blocks, what are the bigger ones?
# eefm - Block Fronts (ah ok also yes..)
# eee - Road Axes (yeah kinda?)
# eecd - Dispersed Hamlet
# esia - Area-type Complementary Services and Information
# (green areas, medians, traffic circles)
# eesil - Line-type Complementary Services and Information
# (rivers, railroads, roads, trails, paths)
# eesip -
# Point-type Complementary Services and Information
# (municipal buildings or administrative offices, parks or gardens)
# eepe - External Polygon (no)
# eepem - External Block Polygon (probably not)
yuc_m_big <- st_read(dsn = here("31_yucatan_2020/conjunto_de_datos"),
                    layer = "31m")

ggsave("clusters_on_yuc_a_clusters.pdf")
```

Ok i think that earlier population count was incorrect -- try again by just overlapping the areas
```{r}
# population for all areas of the city
yuc_m_pop <- yuc_m %>% 
  right_join(yuc_cluster_pops, by = c("CVEGEO", "CVE_ENT", "CVE_MUN",
                                     "CVE_LOC", "CVE_AGEB", "CVE_MZA"))

# now overlap these populations counts with the shapefiles for the clusters
clusters <- st_transform(clusters, st_crs(yuc_m_pop))
intersections <- st_intersection(yuc_m_pop, clusters)

# great NOW i can go by TIRS cluster and block to see what the population of each is
pop_cluster <- intersections %>% 
  group_by(CLUSTER, MZTIRS) %>% 
  summarize(Block_Population = sum(POBTOT))
pop_block <- intersections %>% 
  group_by(CLUSTER) %>% 
  summarize(Block_Population = sum(POBTOT))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = intersections, linewidth = 0.05) +
 # geom_sf(data = yuc_fm, linewidth = 0.005, color = "red") +
  geom_sf(data = clusters, linewidth = 0.005, color = "blue")
ggsave("clusters_pop.pdf")
```

SINAVE Data
```{r}
s21 <- season21 %>% 
  # only want data for Merida (050 MUNICIPO_RES and 31 ENTIDAD_RES)
  filter(MUNICIPIO_RES == 50 & ENTIDAD_RES == 31) %>% 
  # change symptom onset date to match cases dataset (i.e., weeks since 
  #  start of ABD season)
  mutate(Week_onset = ymd(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS),
         Week_onset = epiweek(Week_onset), #epiweek????
         Year = year(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS)) %>% 
  relocate(c(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS, Week_onset), .before = ID_REGISTRO)

s22 <- season22 %>% 
  # only want data for Merida (050 MUNICIPO_RES and 31 ENTIDAD_RES)
  filter(MUNICIPIO_RES == 50 & ENTIDAD_RES == 31) %>% 
  # change symptom onset date to match cases dataset (i.e., weeks since 
  #  start of ABD season)
  mutate(Week_onset = ymd(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS),
         Week_onset = epiweek(Week_onset), #epiweek????
         Year = year(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS)) %>%
  relocate(c(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS, Week_onset), .before = ID_REGISTRO)

s23 <- season23 %>% 
  # only want data for Merida (050 MUNICIPO_RES and 31 ENTIDAD_RES)
  filter(MUNICIPIO_RES == 50 & ENTIDAD_RES == 31) %>% 
  # change symptom onset date to match cases dataset (i.e., weeks since 
  #  start of ABD season)
  mutate(Week_onset = ymd(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS),
         Week_onset = epiweek(Week_onset), #epiweek????
         Year = year(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS)) %>%
  relocate(c(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS, Week_onset), .before = ID_REGISTRO)
```

By source

```{r}
ggplot() +

          alpha = 0.85) +

          aes(color = as.factor(Source))) +
```

# Table 1
Formatting
```{r}
cases$Arm_1TIRS <- 
  factor(cases$Arm_1TIRS, levels = c(0, 1),
         labels = c("Control",
                    "TIRS Intervention"))
cases$Year <- factor(cases$Year)
cases$Age <- as.numeric(cases$Age)

label(cases$Age) <- "Age"
label(cases$Arm_1TIRS) <- "Trial Arm"
label(cases$Year) <- "Year*"
label(cases$Week_onset) <- "Week of Symptom Onset <sup>†</sup>"

footnote <- "*In 2023, there was a large outbreak of DENV-3 <br> <sup>†</sup> Week of the year"
```

Make Table
```{r}
case_tab <- table1(~ Age + Year + Arm_1TIRS + Week_onset | Source, data = cases,
       footnote=footnote)
case_tab <- as.data.frame(case_tab)
print(xtable(case_tab, type = "latex"), file = "case_tab.tex")
```

# Case Data over Time
Combine all SINAVE data? all data in general? 
```{r}
sinave <- do.call("rbind", list(s21, s22, s23))

table(sinave$ESTATUS_CASO) # 1 likely; 2 confirmed; 3 discarded

# we want only confirmed cases? (ESTATUS_CASO == 2)
sinave_cases <- sinave %>% 
  filter(ESTATUS_CASO == 2)
```

and get case counts
```{r}
sinave_case_num <- sinave_cases %>% 
  count(Year, Week_onset) %>% 
  mutate(Year = as.character(Year))
trial_case_num <- cases %>% 
  count(Year, Week_onset) %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  mutate(Year = as.character(Year)) %>% 
  add_row(Year = "2021", Week_onset = 1, n = 0)
```

With same y axis
```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_col(data = sinave_case_num,
           aes(x = Week_onset, y = n, fill = "SINAVE"),
           alpha = 0.6) + 
  geom_col(data = trial_case_num,
           aes(x = Week_onset, y = n, fill = "TIRS")) +
  facet_wrap(~ Year, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TIRS" = "steelblue",
                               "SINAVE" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(x = "Week of Symptom Onset",
       y = "Number of Cases",
       fill = "Source",
       title = "ABD Cases by Week (TIRS vs. SINAVE)") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1, 53, by = 2)
  ) +
  theme_classic()
ggsave("cases_by_week.pdf")
```
